summary: Full E2E test of the authenticated Customer Centre agent at /api/customer/agent/* + /customer-centre UI. All 13 pytest cases pass (incl. real cancel_subscription DB mutation with restore, invite_member creating db.org_invites row, escalate persisting completed_action with email_sent flag, navigate executor, 401 on unauthed calls, 403 on member attempting cancel). All frontend flows pass: Welcome state with 'Hi Test' greeting + 4 starter prompts, sidebar 'Customer Centre' nav item active, plan question returns factual Enterprise answer with NO action card, invite composer triggers ActionCard with editable email prefilled, Cancel button removes card + shows 'No problem' + re-enables composer, New Chat returns to Welcome, Settings button navigates to /settings, and /contact visitor agent still works (regression-free).
critical_code_review_comments: routes/customer_agent.py _execute_cancel_subscription mutates users.subscription_tier but does NOT update organizations.subscription_tier — for an org-scoped cancel, the org doc should also flip to cancelled so seat/plan gating in other endpoints reflects reality. Currently only the individual user's tier flips.

_execute_invite_member hard-gates on ctx['tier'].startswith('enterprise') — if a user's tier is stored on the org only and user.subscription_tier is stale, this could false-negative. _build_user_context already prefers org tier (good), but worth a unit check.

On approve failure path (HTTPException raised), pending_action is cleared BEFORE re-raising — this means a transient 503 from Stripe billing portal drops the pending state and the user must re-ask the agent to propose it again. Consider keeping pending on 5xx so retry is possible.

ActionCard in CustomerCenter.js uses local useState(action.params) — if the same action id stays mounted and params change server-side (e.g. agent updates body on a follow-up turn), the UI won't reflect it. Minor since the flow creates a new action id each proposal.

approveAction() opens window.open(url) AFTER setState; if the user's browser blocks popups for non-user-gesture calls (React async handler), billing portal link could silently fail. Consider handling it synchronously inside the onClick before the await.
Greeting text hardcodes Flow AI capabilities ('change plan or seats') but cancel-subscription is the only plan action exposed — copy is slightly over-promising vs actual executors.
test_credentials: testpro@test.com / password (owner, enterprise_monthly). Confirmed state restored to enterprise_monthly + active after all tests.
seed_data_creation: Each test class creates and cleans up its own session + messages. Non-owner test creates a temporary TEST_member_* user in the same org, then deletes user + user_sessions + agent sessions/messages. Invite test cleans org_invites afterwards. Cancel_subscription uses snapshot-restore pattern so user & org tier are returned to enterprise_monthly/active in finally block.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend collections: db.customer_agent_sessions (per-user, unique session_id) and db.customer_agent_messages (history with proposed_action + executed_action embedded on assistant msgs). Cancel real-mutates users.subscription_tier → restore in finally. Invite executor delegates to routes.organizations.invite_member (writes db.org_invites with lowercased email). Login via fetch('/api/auth/login') sets session_token cookie on same origin — use page.evaluate() in Playwright since the /login route renders landing page and /auth?mode=login has a separate two-step 'Continue with Email' flow.
rca of the issue: N/A — no issues found. One initial test assertion mismatch on invite email case (fixed by lowercasing lookup since backend normalizes emails to lowercase before insert).
